name: British 800-style 50 W (master volume)
notes: Early-80s British master volume style: the classic 80s rock and metal crunch. Path: V1a input stage -> gain pot with bright cap -> V1b (cold, 10k cathode) -> V2a -> cathode follower -> tone stack -> master volume -> phase inverter -> 2x EL34 with feedback and presence. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): 12AX7 stages with 100k plate resistors, V1a cathode 2.7k with 0.68 uF (bass cut below about 90 Hz), V1b with a 10k unbypassed cathode (cold, lower gain), tone stack 470p/22n/22n/33k/220k/1M/25k (the 'british' values), EL34 pair into 3.4k. UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: bright cap on the gain pot as a +8 dB shelf at 800 Hz; the 470k/470p network after V1b as -6 dB plus a 150 Hz high-pass; V1b bias -2.6 V; V2a partial bypass as a -4 dB shelf; the cathode follower as a custom curve (top 40 V); the 10k unbypassed cathode's local feedback is not modelled (only its cold bias); feedback amount (set for about 7 dB). Phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage). POWER SUPPLY: silicon rectifier: only the transformer winding, as 80 ohm into 50 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.) COUPLING: every coupling capacitor and the output transformer's low end are 1st-order high-passes (highpass1), as in the real circuit; each gain stage ends with its coupling capacitor into the next grid resistor (coupling_nf, grid_ohms; default 22 nF into 1 Mohm = 7.2 Hz). The cathode follower is DC-coupled to v2a's plate and drives the tone stack directly (coupling_nf 0 on both): the DC shift of hard clipping moves the cathode follower's working point, and the tone stack's capacitors block it. PREAMP SUPPLY: every gain stage (v1a, v1b, v2a, cathode_follower, pi) hangs on the same supply through decoupling filters (preamp_targets), so it sags too, about 100 ms behind (preamp_filter_ms: a GUESS; real amps have 10k-ish resistors and 10-50 uF capacitors per node).
